A.explanation: At balance the p.d. across $QP$ equals $0.50\text{ V}$, which is $1/4$ of the $2.0\text{ V}$ across $QR$, so $QP = QR/4$ for the uniform wire.

B.explanation: This would give $0.67\text{ V}$ across $QP$ if the $2.0\text{ V}$ were shared proportionally, which is larger than the $0.50\text{ V}$ e.m.f. of X.

C.explanation: This would give $1.33\text{ V}$ across $QP$, much larger than $0.50\text{ V}$, and confuses the $0.50$ to $2.0$ ratio.

D.explanation: This would give $1.50\text{ V}$ across $QP$, which is three times the balance voltage needed to oppose cell X.

hints: Notice the galvanometer reads zero at P, so the p.d. across length $QP$ of the wire must exactly balance the approximately $0.50\text{ V}$ e.m.f. of cell X.
Recall the wire QR is uniform and connected across the $2.0\text{ V}$ driver cell, so p.d. is proportional to length with $2.0\text{ V}$ across the full length $QR$.
Compare $0.50\text{ V}$ to $2.0\text{ V}$ as a fraction and apply the same fraction to length $QR$ to locate $QP$.
walkthrough: At the null point the current in the galvanometer branch is zero, so the p.d. between Q and P on the resistance wire balances the e.m.f. of X: $V_{QP} \approx 0.50\text{ V}$.
The driver circuit puts the full driver e.m.f. across the uniform wire because internal resistance is negligible, so $V_{QR} = 2.0\text{ V}$.
For a uniform wire, resistance and p.d. are proportional to length: $V_{QP}/V_{QR} = QP/QR$.
Hence $QP \approx QR/4$. This is option A.
